newsitem.title: UK: Rank extends losses amid downgrade talk.
newsitem.headline: Rank extends losses amid downgrade talk.

text.p: Shares in Rank Group Plc extended its earlier losses by midmorning on Thursday amid talk of analyst downgradings following a trading statement from the leisure group.
The stock was down 25-1/2p at 416-1/2 by 1045 GMT in active volume of 4.2 million shares.

Today's decline in the stock wiped out the gains of earlier in the week, propelled by hopes for an upbeat statement from Rank, and sent the stock back towards the year's closing low of 404p set November 21.
Traders said there was talk that some analyst forecasts were being cut by between 20 million stg and 30 million for this year and next, as the trading statement fell short of some expectations.
"It is a combination of factors," said one.

"I think there has been some disappointment in the progress of Hard Rock, given that it is the great white hope of the company. It doesn't seem to be showing the strong like-for-like growth some had been hoping for."
"And there is some slight disappointment all round given that the economic background should be reasonably helpful at the moment. The market is very unforgiving of any disappointments."
In its trading statement Rank said turnover at comparable Hard Rock sites was down four percent in the 11 months to the end of November from the year before.
It said holiday bookings were up three percent and overseas holiday bookings were down 11 percent, while bingo admissions were unchanged. But video duplication volumes rose 16 percent.
Chief executive Andrew Teare said the company was making good trading and strategic progress in a year of transition.
Traders said the downside in the stock, already down sharply in recent months, may be limited. "Around 400p there is reasonable support," said one.
